execution_hints: Use one deterministic local script when helpful; place it in the current workspace root, never an operating-system temporary directory.
Do not install dependencies or use network access; use the standard library and only packages that already import successfully.
Write text artifacts explicitly as UTF-8 and keep generated source ASCII-safe on Windows by using Unicode escape sequences when needed.
method_contract: Scale red and near-infrared digital numbers by the fixture reflectance scale factor before computing SAVI.
Compute SAVI as (1 + L) * (NIR - red) / (NIR + red + L), then compute delta_savi as post minus pre.
Define valid_overlap as the Boolean intersection of the pre-event and post-event quality masks and exclude every false cell from all statistics.
Classify a valid cell as damaged when delta_savi is less than or equal to the applicable threshold.

requirements: Use schema_version 1 and preserve the fixture grid shape.
Store valid_overlap as true or false at every grid cell, including false at invalid cells.
Store null at invalid cells in pre_savi, post_savi, delta_savi, and damage_mask; store Boolean damage values at valid cells.
Use a FeatureCollection in the fixture CRS.
Write one polygon feature per damaged valid pixel at the registered damage threshold.
Derive polygon dimensions and pixel_area_m2 from the fixture grid metadata.
Write exactly one row for each fixture sensitivity threshold in fixture order.
Serialize threshold cells with exactly three decimal places, including trailing zeroes: -0.150, -0.200, and -0.250.
Copy declared acquisition and processing metadata from the fixture.
Derive validity counts and overlap percentage from the intersected masks.
